findings.reason: §2's deliverable is "waits or is refused", which a lease can only half of, so the reuse decision changes the endpoint's stated semantics, not just its implementation.
findings.text: `HostLease` already implements cross-host single-owner exclusion in the fleet's shared state directory (atomic `os.link`, renewable, 30 s stale window) and is the mechanism `reckon/crew/promotion.py:340` uses to exclude a promotion on another host; the plan cites only the §8 lease precedent in prose and never establishes that this owner cannot serve §2, so a node briefed from the plan can build a second cross-node exclusion primitive beside the one the fleet already runs. Note for the brief: `HostLease.claim` reattaches when holder identity (host, pid, job, pid-namespace) matches, so two threads of one process both succeed — it cannot satisfy §2's "exclusion between two holders inside one process (two threads…) is no weaker than today's", and its non-blocking claim plus 30 s stale window mean it can refuse but cannot wait, while §2 asks for "waits or is refused". The review's reading is that §2 needs a POSIX record lock (`lockf`, which §1 measured as cross-node on GPFS and which appears nowhere in `reckon/` today) for the wait path, and that its relation to `HostLease` — extends, sits beside, or is scoped to plan state only — is the decision the brief must settle.

findings.reason: making the module mandatory (instead of optional) changes what the node builds and what §4's followups point at, and the 74-vs-42 mismatch would let a census pass at the wrong row count.
findings.text: the lock wrapper the plan proposes to change in place is one of about twenty copies of the same shape; each opens a path, takes `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)`, yields, and unlocks in `finally`, and each resolves its own lock directory: `reckon/project_state.py:302` (`docs/.reckon/locks`), `reckon/_store.py:395` (`_serialized_path_lock`, config-home `locks/<namespace>`), `reckon/ledger.py:2500`, `reckon/compliance.py:145`, `reckon/crew/runs.py:480` (`_pointer_lock`, with the blocking flag §2 will need), `reckon/crew/placement.py:176`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_peer.py:222`, `reckon/crew/admission/service.py:46`, `reckon/crew/budget_reset.py:101`, `reckon/crew/resumption.py:546` and `:2386`, `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:226`, `reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:582`, `reckon/crew/model_catalogue.py:292`, `reckon/crew/picker/outcomes.py:280`, `reckon/crew/obligations.py:3320`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:501`, `reckon/crew/session_host.py:555`, `reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:654` and `:822`, `reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:1880`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2453`, `reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:392`. §2 says "one new module under `reckon/` *if* the lock is factored out" — the conditional leaves every one of these keeping `flock`, so §4's census will then file them as "needs the §2 lock" one row at a time in followups rather than against one owner. A second counting defect in the same census: §1 says the primitive "appears 74 times in 23 modules", which is every `fcntl.flock` reference — measured here as 42 call sites that take a lock, 31 that only release, and one `flags =` assignment at `reckon/crew/runs.py:490`. §4 correctly defines a row as a *taking* call (release-only is excluded), so the row population is 42, not the 74 a worker reading §1 would target.

findings.reason: the section must say, in its own text, that the new module absorbs the existing lock wrappers or why it cannot, and that is a sentence the plan does not currently contain.
findings.text: §2's write paths add "one new module under `reckon/` if the lock is factored out" plus a probe script under `scripts/`, and the section names neither a definition it retires nor a merge, nor states why nothing can be; the trees already carry the surface the module would replace (the twenty wrappers above, each a private helper, and the `public_definitions` count of 2606 is the family this would add to).

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the endpoint hides cross-node exclusion, lock placement and the wait-or-refuse policy behind the one `_resource_lock` context manager (`reckon/project_state.py:302`), an interface smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the flock wrapper over `open`/`flock(LOCK_EX)`/`yield`/`unlock` exists in 20 modules under `reckon/`, and the plan's §2 makes a shared owner optional rather than naming one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2606, cli_options 484, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §2 adds "one new module under `reckon/`" and its public definitions without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's §2 proposes cross-node exclusion without naming `reckon/crew/host_lease.py:41`, the existing cross-host claim the fleet already uses in `reckon/crew/promotion.py:340`, although §1 of the plan cites the lease precedent in prose.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the change extends the existing per-resource lock context manager in place, rather than layering a parallel lock beside it; the probe script is specified to go "through the production lock code" rather than re-deriving the lock path.
